name: Lambert Conformal Conic (2SP) edge cases — negative-n inverse quadrant fix and the degenerate single-parallel branch

source.document: Snyder, J. P. (1987) USGS PP-1395 §14; EPSG Geomatics Guidance Note 7-2 §1.3.2.1 (Lambert Conic Conformal 2SP) inverse
source.page: PP-1395 §14 (forward/inverse); EPSG GN7-2 §1.3.2.1 inverse (ρ = ±√…, sign of n)
source.file: scripts/verify_lcc.py (independent Python reference, validated against the EPSG GN7-2 worked example)
source.notes: SYNTHETIC edge-case zones — not real country-config zones, so this fixture is skipped by the registry cross-check. These cases exercise code paths the real US SPCS zones (all n > 0) cannot reach: (1) southern-hemisphere 2SP with n < 0, which previously made the inverse recover θ ∓ π (a ~π/|n| ≈ 280° longitude error) until the inverse was fixed to θ = atan2(sign(n)·(E−FE), sign(n)·(ρ₀−(N−FN))); (2) an equatorial straddle with small |n| ≈ 0.088; (3) the degenerate φ₁ = φ₂ branch in both hemispheres. All values cross-checked with scripts/verify_lcc.py.

projection.method: Lambert Conformal Conic (2SP, EPSG::9802) — synthetic edge-case variants

cases.name: Southern 2SP (35°S / 45°S) — n ≈ −0.6436 < 0
cases.notes: n < 0 ⇒ F < 0 ⇒ ρ < 0. The raw atan2(E−FE, ρ₀−(N−FN)) returned θ ∓ π (a 279.7 km longitude drift) before the sign(n) θ fix.

cases.name: Equatorial straddle (5°N / 15°S) — n ≈ −0.0876 < 0, small |n|
cases.notes: Small negative n stresses the θ quadrant fix with |1/n| large.

cases.name: Single parallel φ₁=φ₂=34°N — degenerate branch, n = sin 34° ≈ +0.5592 > 0
cases.notes: φ₁ = φ₂ triggers the EPSG 1SP limit n = sin φ₁ instead of the ln m / ln t ratio.

cases.name: Single parallel φ₁=φ₂=34°S — degenerate branch, n ≈ −0.5592 < 0
cases.notes: Degenerate branch AND n < 0 — the only case exercising both code paths at once.

roundtrip_test.description: Forward then inverse must reproduce the input geographic coordinates to within 1e-9 deg (~0.1 mm).
